Recall $d \sin\theta_n = n\lambda$ for normal incidence with $\lambda = 5.50 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$, and that the semicircular screen collects all forward directions up to $\theta = 90^{\circ}$.
Require the highest visible order to have $\sin\theta \le 1$ while the next order has $\sin\theta > 1$, giving an inequality $n\lambda \le d < (n+1)\lambda$ to test.
walkthrough: A total of 9 dots means 1 central zero-order dot plus 4 dots on each side, so the maximum visible order is $n_{max} = 4$.
Use the grating equation for normal incidence: $d \sin\theta_n = n\lambda$ with $\lambda = 5.50 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$.
For $n=4$ to exist on the forward semicircle, $\sin\theta_4 = 4\lambda/d \le 1$, so $d \ge 4\lambda = 4 \times 5.50 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m} = 2.20 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$.
For $n=5$ not to exist, $\sin\theta_5 = 5\lambda/d > 1$, so $d < 5\lambda = 5 \times 5.50 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m} = 2.75 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$.
Only $2.25 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$ lies in this range. This is option A.
